sections.label: NPF spending and funded projects
sections.summary: About half of NPF spending went to productivity improvement projects and half to CET programmes, including sector-specific and transformation schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: About half was spent on productivity improvement projects and the other half was spent on CET programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Some of the larger projects funded by the NPF include sector-specific schemes like the Construction Productivity and Capability Fund, as well as schemes that support enterprise and workforce transformation like the Inclusive Growth Programme and the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: In identifying areas for productivity improvement, sector agencies take into account feedback from the industry, best practices from Singapore and globally, as well as relevant benchmarking studies.

sections.label: Labour productivity growth rate
sections.summary: Labour productivity growth was 2.6% per annum in the five years before COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Our labour productivity growth rate was 2.6% per annum in the last five years, prior to COVID-19.

sections.label: Plan completion and grant disbursed
sections.summary: The plan was completed in March 2022, with $1.36 million of grant disbursed from 2016 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The plan was completed in March 2022, just last year, with a $1.36 million of grant disbursed for a duration of 2016 to 2022.

sections.label: NPF funding to agencies only
sections.summary: The NPF only funds other Government agencies and programmes, not TACs or companies directly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: First, to confirm my understanding, the NPF, if I read the Minister of State correctly, only funds other Government agencies and programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: It does not give funding directly to TACs or to companies.

sections.label: NPF use and project monitoring
sections.summary: Ministries and agencies can tap the NPF for productivity and CET projects, and NPF-funded projects are regularly monitored against targets and KPIs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The NPF is available for the Ministries and agencies to tap into to spearhead productivity enhancement projects and CET that will benefit the TACs and the sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For the second question, as our companies and workers benefit from a wide range of schemes, in addition to the NPF, the various schemes are also subject to scrutiny.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to assure him that within the NPF, we regularly monitor the progress of the project that is funded by NPF to ensure they meet project level targets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For example, the hotel productivity plan I shared.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We will monitor how they have met the targets and the KPIs, item by item, such as number of firms or individuals who benefited from the projects.
